a: State expected metric change and why before starting an experiment.
Compute required sample size from baseline, MDE, and power.
Sample Ratio Mismatch means assignment is biased — investigate.
Repeated early looks inflate false positives; use sequential methods or fixed horizon.
Watch secondary metrics that must not degrade (errors, latency, revenue).
Short-term lifts may fade as users adapt.
Social products may need cluster randomization to avoid interference.
Log exposures so analysis only includes assigned users who saw the experience.
Long-term holdouts measure cumulative impact of many changes.
Ship when primary metric wins with acceptable guardrails and practical significance.
